target_customer: Data analysts, engineers and data teams who write SQL
problem: SQL tools were single-user and clunky, with no easy way to share, organise and collaborate on queries and results.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat subscription with a free tier

founders.name: Rahil Sondhi
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Feb 2022): coded since age 10, engineer at Instacart in 2017 where the idea came from. Tigerdata says he co-founded with an unnamed friend.

technical_complexity.rationale: Desktop and web SQL editor with real-time collaboration and connectors to many databases. Standard engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Saved queries, shared folders and a data catalog create some lock-in, but editors and BI tools with SQL features were numerous and copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it decisively; Timescale bought it in 2024, moved it to limited support in September 2025, and a retirement date of September 1, 2026 was reported.

market_need_then: Founder wrote SQL daily at Instacart and found tools lacked sharing and collaboration; customers grew from about 300 to over 2,000 between 2020 and 2022 without outbound sales.

branding.domain_note: popsql.com. Trademark filed December 2018, registered September 2020, now owned by Timescale per a trademark aggregator.

identity.voice_and_tone: Casual and developer friendly; comparison pages against Mode and Redash

branding.community_and_virality: Growth described as product-led with no outbound sales; one blogger noted it is pronounced like popsicle, which is not a stated origin.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable, pronounceable name that fit the playful positioning, and wide team usage, but no brand-specific press or community found.

outcome_analysis: PopSQL grew by product-led adoption to more than 2,000 companies by February 2022 on a $3.4M seed and $14M Series A, then was acquired by Timescale on April 4, 2024 at an undisclosed price. The product moved to limited support in September 2025 and retirement was reported for September 1, 2026, so the exit looks like a team and product absorption rather than a lasting standalone business.
notes: Founder education not found. No competitor sources dated near 2019 were found; later comparison pages name Mode, Redash, Metabase and DBeaver. Totals reported by aggregators range from $17.4M (TechCrunch) to $18.55M; no earlier rounds are itemised. Limited-support and September 2026 retirement come from search results and the PopSQL blog URL, which was not opened. Failure factor is a soft inference from the limited-support notice.
